x: The First Plan (1951–56) used the Harrod–Domar model, which ties growth to savings and investment. The Second Plan used the Mahalanobis model.
t: Discriminate the models of the First and Second Plans.

x: Option B is incorrect: the First Plan put agriculture first, along with food, rehabilitation after Partition, and price stability. Heavy industry was the Second Plan's priority.
t: Discriminate the First and Second Plans' priorities.

x: The first industrial policy of independent India came in 1948, the second in 1956, liberalisation in 1991, and the first cotton mill (Fort Gloster) in 1818. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Arrange the industrial milestones in time order.

x: Both are true: the National Planning Committee (1938, under Nehru) was the first planning effort before Independence, and planned development began on 1 April 1951.
t: Recall the planning start dates.

x: Agriculture is the primary sector, the First Plan led to the Community Development Programme (1952), the Second Plan used the Mahalanobis model, and Shyama Prasad Mukherjee announced the 1948 policy. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each item to its detail.

x: The 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution brought in the idea of a joint sector, with public and private ownership together. The 1948 policy set up the mixed economy.
t: Discriminate the 1948 and 1956 policies.

x: The 1991 New Economic Policy brought in all three: liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation (LPG).
t: Recall what LPG stands for.

x: Cottage industry was the first industry to develop in India, long before modern mills. The first cotton mill came only in 1818.
t: Discriminate traditional from modern industry.

x: Option C is incorrect: the first cotton mill at Fort Gloster near Kolkata came in 1818, not 1951. 1951 is the start of the First Plan.
t: Match each event to its year.

x: The Second Plan (1956–61) aimed at rapid industrialisation through heavy and basic industries, using the Mahalanobis model.
t: Match each Plan to its focus.

x: Option B is incorrect: the Eleventh Plan (2007–12) aimed at faster and more inclusive growth. 'Growth with social justice' was the Ninth Plan's aim.
t: Match each Plan to its focus.

x: Both are true: the Fifth Plan (1974–79) focused on Garibi Hatao, jobs, justice and self-reliance. Its dates do not explain its aims, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a period explains a focus.

x: The First Plan focused on agriculture, the Fourth on growth with stability and self-reliance, the Sixth on growth and poverty reduction, and the Ninth on growth with social justice. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Match each Plan to its focus.

x: The order is the National Planning Committee (1938), the Bombay and Gandhian Plans (1944), the People's Plan (1945) and the First Plan (1951). The answer is B, D, A, C.
t: Arrange the pre-Plan schemes in time order.

x: Both are true: J.P. Narayan's Sarvodaya Plan came in 1950, and annual plans ran in 1990–92, between the Seventh and Eighth Plans.
t: Recall the gap years between Plans.

x: The First Plan ran 1951–56, the Third 1961–66, the Plan Holiday 1966–69, and the Seventh 1985–90. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each Plan to its period.

x: All four are correct: the Third Plan aimed at agriculture and self-reliance, the Plan Holiday used annual plans, and the Seventh Plan focused on growth, jobs and productivity.
t: Match each Plan to its focus.

x: The Planning Commission was set up on 15 March 1950 by a Cabinet resolution. NITI Aayog replaced it on 1 January 2015.
t: Discriminate 1950 from 2015.

x: The Planning Commission was a non-constitutional body set up by Cabinet resolution, while the Finance Commission is a constitutional body under Article 280. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
t: Discriminate constitutional from executive bodies.

x: Both are true: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission, and it was set up by a Cabinet resolution. How it was created does not explain why it replaced the old body, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether the method of creation explains the purpose.

x: B is the keyed answer, but the Planning Commission was in fact a permanent, non-statutory advisory body. The contrast is with the Finance Commission, which is set up afresh every five years. As written, all four statements are true.
t: Discriminate a permanent body from a periodic one.

x: Both are true: under the old system, the Planning Commission allocated Plan resources and the Finance Commission non-Plan resources.
t: Discriminate Plan from non-Plan transfers.

x: Both are true: the Planning Commission was called quasi-political, and it was set up by Cabinet resolution. Its legal basis does not explain its political character, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a legal basis explains a character.

x: The Planning Commission handled planning and allocating resources, and the Finance Commission handles tax sharing and grants. The answer is a-ii, b-i.
t: Match each body to its function.

x: NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015 by a Cabinet resolution. Its DMEO was set up on 18 September 2015.
t: Discriminate NITI Aayog's date from DMEO's.

x: Option B is incorrect as per NITI's 2015 set-up: the UT Chief Ministers on the Governing Council were Delhi's and Puducherry's. Other UTs are represented by Lt Governors, and the PM chairs it.
t: Recall the UTs with legislatures in 2015.

x: Both are true: NITI Aayog gives States a bigger say in policy because it works through cooperative federalism and a bottom-up approach. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the approach explains the outcome.

x: NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015, DMEO on 18 September 2015, Arvind Panagariya was the first Vice-Chairman, and NITI means National Institution for Transforming India. The answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each item to its detail.

x: All three are correct: DMEO is an attached office of NITI Aayog, formed by merging the Programme Evaluation Organisation and the Independent Evaluation Office, to monitor and evaluate government schemes.
t: Recall the origin and role of DMEO.

x: Both are true: NITI Aayog was created by a Cabinet resolution, and it replaced the Planning Commission. Replacing a body does not explain how NITI was created, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether replacement explains the method.

x: Option C is incorrect: NITI Aayog is a public-policy think tank that replaced the Planning Commission and follows cooperative federalism. It is not the Planning Commission.
t: Discriminate NITI Aayog from the Planning Commission.

x: All four are part of NITI Aayog's structure: the Vice-Chairperson, full-time members, ex-officio members and special invitees, with the PM as chair.
t: Recall NITI Aayog's structure.

x: DMEO is the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office, attached to NITI Aayog.
t: Expand the short name.

x: The UNDP published the first Human Development Report in 1990, prepared by Mahbub-ul-Haq.
t: Recall the first HDR year.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Railway Budget was merged with the General Budget in 2017–18, not 2015–16. That year the Budget date also moved to 1 February.
t: Recall the merger year.

x: Both are true: the First Plan and the First Finance Commission both date from 1951. Happening in the same year does not make one explain the other, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether the same year means one causes the other.

x: The first KVK dates from 1974, the first RRB 1975, NABARD 1982 and the first private mutual fund 1993. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Arrange the institutions in time order.

x: B is keyed, but the dates give the order Pantnagar (1960), the Green Revolution (1966–67), bank nationalisation (1969) and the first KVK (1974): A, C, B, D. That order is not among the options.
t: Arrange the events by year.

x: Both are true: the HDI was developed by Mahbub-ul-Haq, with Amartya Sen among its key thinkers.
t: Recall the founders of the HDI.

x: The National Planning Committee dates from 1938, the first Industrial Policy and IFCI from 1948, and the RBI's nationalisation from 1949. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-ii, d-iii.
t: Allow two items to share a year.

x: The groundwork for the First Finance Commission was laid in 1949. The Commission itself was set up in 1951.
t: Discriminate preparation from constitution.

x: The Community Development Programme dates from 1952, SBI and ICICI from 1955, and the Second Industrial Policy from 1956. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-ii, d-iii.
t: Allow two items to share a year.

x: The Second Plan began in 1956, the same year as the Industrial Policy Resolution.
t: Recall the Second Plan year.

x: IDBI and UTI were set up in 1964, the Dandekar–Rath poverty study came in 1971, and the first Food for Work programme in 1977–78. The answer is a-i, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.
t: Allow two items to share a year.

x: All four are correct: Antyodaya began in Rajasthan in 1977–78, IRDP was tried in 1978–79 and went national in 1980, and the second bank nationalisation was in 1980.
t: Recall the late-1970s schemes.

x: DWCRA dates from 1982, JRY 1989, SIDBI 1990 and the New Economic Policy 1991. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Arrange the schemes in time order.

x: The first green bond was issued in 2007, by the European Investment Bank, and the first BRIC summit was held in 2009. The answer is a-i, b-ii.
t: Match each first to its year.

x: Both are true: the NSE set up its first dedicated debt platform in 2013, and K.V. Kamath became the first President of the New Development Bank in 2015.
t: Recall the BRICS-era firsts.

x: Jim O'Neill of Goldman Sachs coined 'BRIC' in 2001. The first summit was in 2009, and South Africa joined in 2010.
t: Discriminate the coinage from the first summit.
